title: SAF Declares White Nile State Fully Cleared of RSF — Strategic Milestone as RSF Remnants Retreat to Bara
detail: Sudan's Armed Forces announced that White Nile State has been fully cleared of Rapid Support Forces presence, with RSF remnants regrouping in Bara, North Kordofan, following their expulsion from the last positions they held in the state. White Nile State — which runs south of Khartoum along the White Nile river, encompassing cities including Rabak (state capital), Kosti, and Kenana — had been a repeated target of RSF drone strikes throughout April and early May 2026, including the April 3 dual strikes on Al-Jabalain Hospital (10 killed, 7 medical staff), the April 29 attack on SAF's 18th Infantry Division HQ in Kosti, and the May 3 and May 5 strikes on Kenana fuel and industrial facilities. However, SAF maintained ground control of White Nile State throughout the conflict; the clearance announcement indicates SAF has now expelled or neutralized remaining RSF ground elements and irregular units operating in the state's rural areas. The strategic significance is substantial: White Nile State connects Khartoum to South Kordofan and Blue Nile State, providing SAF's primary logistical corridor southward. With White Nile State cleared, SAF's supply lines to the Kordofan and Blue Nile fronts are secured. RSF forces reportedly retreating to Bara in North Kordofan join a larger RSF reconsolidation effort there; Bara has been a contested hub in North Kordofan throughout 2025–2026, but RSF control of the town is increasingly precarious given SAF's multi-front pressure. The clearance announcement came the same week as the SAF Security Council commendation of gains in South Kordofan, Blue Nile, and Darfur, and within days of the Treaty of Jeddah humanitarian framework signing (May 20), reinforcing SAF's political-military posture that total victory is achievable without the need for a comprehensive ceasefire.

media.caption: SAF announces White Nile State fully cleared of RSF presence (May 22, 2026); RSF remnants regrouping in Bara, North Kordofan

title: RSF/SPLM-N Drone Strike Destroys Dilling Medical Warehouses — Six Injured, Thousands Deprived of Medicines
detail: An armed drone strike by RSF/SPLM-N forces on Dilling, South Kordofan, struck and completely destroyed the city's medical supply warehouses on Wednesday evening (May 20–21, 2026), injuring at least six people and depriving thousands of patients across the city of medicines and medical supplies. The attack came amid the ongoing cycle of SAF siege breaks and RSF-SPLM-N counterattacks in South Kordofan: SAF broke the Dilling siege for a third time on May 19–20, recapturing Al-Takma and reopening the Dilling–Kadugli road, only for RSF-SPLM-N forces to launch a retaliatory strike on the city's healthcare infrastructure within 24–48 hours. The targeting of medical warehouses is consistent with the RSF and SPLM-N's documented pattern of attacking healthcare infrastructure and humanitarian supply chains to impose famine-pressure on SAF-controlled towns. Dilling, South Kordofan's second-largest city, was already functioning under severe medical shortages during the RSF-SPLM-N siege cycle; the destruction of the warehouses eliminates the city's primary medical supply buffer at a time when the area is formally at IPC Phase 5 catastrophic famine risk (Kadugli) and near-famine conditions (Dilling). The medical warehouses attack also occurred just days after the first supply convoy in four months reached Kadugli (May 20), highlighting the destructive counter-cycle: SAF logistics access gains are immediately targeted by RSF-SPLM-N to prevent consolidation. Sudan Doctors Network, which has repeatedly warned of an El Fasher-scale healthcare catastrophe in South Kordofan, condemned the attack and called for emergency medical resupply. The UN's OHCHR high-alert statement from May 11 documented at least 12 attacks on health facilities in the January–April 2026 period; this strike brings the total higher. The attack exemplifies why the Treaty of Jeddah's civilian protection provisions — signed by both parties just two days prior — have been met with deep skepticism by humanitarian organizations.

media.caption: RSF/SPLM-N drone strike destroys Dilling medical supply warehouses (around May 20–21, 2026), injuring 6 and depriving thousands of medicines just days after SAF broke the city's siege for the third time
